quests.title: The Line Holds
quests.description: Kill Wandering Skeletons, and every Plague-Ridden Wolf you can find, in the fields east of the Bulwark.
quests.accept_text:
So you're the one who walked through my gate without being asked twice, which I like. I'm High Executor Marla Venn, and this wall is mine.

The Dark Lady gave me the Bulwark when there was nothing here but a ditch and a rumour. Everything east of it wants to come west, and none of it has. The Wandering Skeletons walk the King's Road at night as if they still had somewhere to be, and the Plague-Ridden Wolves run the grass on either side of them.

Go out the east gate and thin them. Stay this side of the crossroads. I don't send people past it until I know they'll come back.
quests.turn_in_text:
The wall will sleep a little easier tonight, and so will I, if I slept.

You came back, which puts you ahead of most. I've got harder work further out, if you want it.

quests.title: Andorhal's Gate
quests.description: Kill Andorhal Skeletons and Andorhal Skeletal Archers at the edge of Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
Andorhal was a city when I was alive. I bought bread there. Now it's the Scourge's, right in the middle of the south, and its dead march out to the crossroads every night and come looking for my wall.

The Andorhal Skeletons hold what's left of its gate, and the Andorhal Skeletal Archers stand on the broken walls and shoot anything that comes close. My patrols can't see past them.

Take the road south from the crossroads toward the lake. You'll know Andorhal by the smoke. Come at the archers from the side, because they're watching the road.
quests.turn_in_text:
My patrols can see into the city now, and what they see isn't pretty.

I've got a harder job for you, if you've the stomach for it.

quests.title: The Necromancers of Andorhal
quests.description: Kill Andorhal Necromancers in the ruins of Andorhal and bring back their Necromantic Foci.
quests.accept_text:
The skeletons don't get up on their own. Somebody stands in the ruins and keeps them on their feet, and that somebody is the Andorhal Necromancers.

Each of them carries a focus, a bone rod wound with black wire, and the rod does most of the work. The Royal Apothecary Society would very much like to know how. I would very much like them to stop.

They keep to the middle of Andorhal, among the burned houses. Kill them and bring me the rods. Don't hold one any longer than you have to. You'll see why.
quests.turn_in_text:
They hum, don't they? I hate that.

The Society will take them apart. One more job and Andorhal's ours to watch.

quests.title: The Magistrate
quests.description: Kill Magistrate Andor and the Andorhal Abominations that guard him in Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
I served in Lordaeron's army before I died. The man who signed my commission was Andorhal's magistrate, and he's still there. He died with his city and got up again, and he sits in what's left of the town hall giving orders as if he'd never stopped.

Magistrate Andor, they call him now. The Andorhal Abominations stand guard over him.

He isn't always in the hall, so kill the abominations while you wait. He's stronger than he looks, so bring friends. And I'd rather it was you than me, which is the closest I'll come to admitting anything today.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then he's at rest, and so is Andorhal, for a little while.

He signed my commission once. I'd rather not have watched him do it again.

quests.title: A Dispatch for the Flamekeeper
quests.description: Carry Venn's dispatch across the street to Flamekeeper Rory Callahan, in the Order's quarter of the Bulwark.

objectives.label: Bring Venn's dispatch to Flamekeeper Rory Callahan across the street

quests.accept_text:
Look across my street. Those banners are the Order of the Pale Flame. They used to keep a fort on Sorrow Hill, under the Crusade's nose, until the hill got too dead even for them. Now they're inside my wall.

They wear what used to be Scarlet armour and they're led by newcomers. I don't like them. They also kill the mindless dead and leave my people alone, and a wall needs every friend it can get.

Take this to their Flamekeeper, Rory Callahan. He stands at the keep's door on the south side. It's a short walk, so don't let him keep you talking.
quests.turn_in_text:
Marla Venn's seal. She writes like she's sharpening a knife.

She wants to know if we'll hold the road south of Andorhal. Tell her we will, and that the Order sends its regards, which she'll hate.

on_accept.name: Venn's Dispatch
on_accept.description: A dispatch sealed with the Bulwark's black wax.

quests.title: Felstone Field
quests.description: Kill Felstone Ghouls and Felstone Cultists round the cauldron on the Felstone farm.
quests.accept_text:
Apothecary Dorian Vesk. Don't touch anything on the bench.

The Scourge brews its plague in cauldrons out in the fields, and I want to know what's in them. The nearest is on the Felstone farm, north of the King's Road. The Felstone Cultists tend it, and the Felstone Ghouls who used to work that field stand round it like they're still waiting for the harvest.

Turn north at the crossroads and go past the dead orchard. The cauldron's in the middle of the field. Clear the ghouls and the cultists, and leave the cauldron alone. I want it whole.
quests.turn_in_text:
That'll do nicely. The way in's open now.

Now for the part I actually care about.

quests.title: A Sample from Felstone
quests.description: Kill the Felstone Cauldron Lord and take the Felstone Cauldron Sample it carries.
quests.accept_text:
A sample out of the cauldron itself is no good to me. The cultists add whatever's lying around. The clean stuff, the batch they started from, is in a flask on the belt of the thing that keeps the cauldron.

It's a Felstone Cauldron Lord, one of the Scourge's stitched brutes. It's big and slow and it hits like a falling barn.

It stands at the Felstone cauldron. Put it down and bring me the flask. Keep it upright and keep it out of the sun.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's still warm, and that's wonderful.

There are more cauldrons in the south. I'd like them all.

quests.title: Dalson's Tears
quests.description: Kill Dalson's Ghouls at the Dalson farm and bring back a Dalson's Cauldron Sample from its Cauldron Necrolytes.
quests.accept_text:
The Dalson farm has its own cauldron, and I want to set its brew beside the Felstone one. If they're the same, the Scourge has a recipe. If they're not, it's experimenting, and that's worse.

The Cauldron Necrolytes who stir it carry flasks of the brew. Dalson's Ghouls work the yard round them.

It's north and a little east of Felstone, the farm with the big red barn. Leave the barn alone. I mean that. People go in there and don't come out, and I've only got one of you.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thicker than Felstone's. They're changing the recipe from farm to farm.

That's either very bad or very interesting. I'd like one more before I decide.

quests.title: The Writhing Haunt
quests.description: Kill Haunt Cult Tenders at the Writhing Haunt and bring back a Writhing Haunt Sample.
quests.accept_text:
The last cauldron in the south is at the Writhing Haunt, east of Dalson's. The Haunt Cult Tenders keep it stirred, and the banshees keep everyone else away. I sent an apothecary there last month. He came back without his voice.

I want a sample, and I want the tenders thinned so the next one of us who goes comes back talking.

Go east along the north road until the ground goes soft and the trees die. The tenders carry flasks. The banshees will come when you start fighting, so pick your ground and don't stand in the open.
quests.turn_in_text:
Something's moving in this one. Look at that.

I need someone who knows more about the walking dead than I do, and the only one I trust is on the other side of the sea.

quests.title: What the Plague Is Made Of
quests.description: Carry Vesk's sample case to Apothecary Merrow Vane at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon.

objectives.label: Bring the sample case to Apothecary Merrow Vane at Sun Rock Retreat

quests.accept_text:
I studied under Apothecary Merrow Vane. She's at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon now, watching the dead get up on the Mulgore side of the mountain with nobody calling them. Nobody stirring a cauldron, nobody chanting, they just get up.

I think it's the same sickness as the cauldrons. I'd like to be wrong. Merrow will know.

Take the zeppelin from Tirisfal to Orgrimmar and a wind rider to Sun Rock. She'll be the only Forsaken there. Keep the case upright, and don't let the tauren open it, however politely they ask.
quests.turn_in_text:
These are Dorian's samples, all right. He always did label everything twice.

This one, from the Haunt, moves the way the dead on the Rim move. I'll write to him tonight, and I'm afraid of what I'll be writing.

on_accept.name: Vesk's Sample Case
on_accept.description: A padded case with three labelled flasks. One of them knocks against the side now and then.

quests.title: Cult Couriers
quests.description: Take Cult Courier's Letters from the Haunt Cult Tenders at the Writhing Haunt.
quests.accept_text:
Keep your voice down. I'm Rook, and I watch the Cult of the Damned for the Undercity.

The Cult writes letters. The Haunt Cult Tenders out at the Writhing Haunt carry them off to somebody, folded small enough to hide in a boot, and I'd very much like to know who's reading them.

Only some of the tenders carry one. Bring me what you find, and don't try to read them. The cipher's a nasty one, and the last person who puzzled over it too long started dreaming in it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Every letter's in a different hand, and the same name's in all of them.

I'll need the Undercity to hear this.

quests.title: A Report for the Undercity
quests.description: Carry Rook's report to Deathstalker Rhyne in the Undercity.

objectives.label: Bring Rook's report to Deathstalker Rhyne in the Undercity

quests.accept_text:
The letters name somebody in the Undercity. Somebody who's been passing the Cult our patrol routes, the Bulwark's included.

I won't trust the bats with this, and I won't trust a courier I haven't met. I've met you.

Go out the west gate, back through Tirisfal and down into the Undercity. Deathstalker Rhyne is in the Royal Quarter. Put it in his hand and nobody else's, and don't stop for a drink on the way. Whoever that name belongs to drinks in the same places you would.
quests.turn_in_text:
So this is Rook's report. She writes like she's afraid of running out of ink.

This name's going to make some people very unhappy. Thank you. I'll handle it from here.

on_accept.name: Rook's Report
on_accept.description: A thin report sealed twice, once with wax and once with something that smells like poison.

quests.title: The Mother of the Haunt
quests.description: Kill the Mother of the Haunt and the Haunt Banshees at the Writhing Haunt.
quests.accept_text:
The banshees at the Writhing Haunt answer to something. I call her the Mother of the Haunt. She's old enough to remember the farm before the plague, and she keeps the Haunt Banshees, and the banshees keep the Cult's tenders safe.

While she's there, nobody gets near that cauldron without losing their voice. I want her silenced.

She drifts through the Haunt and she isn't always there. Thin the banshees while you wait for her. When she wails, back off and let it pass. You'll know it when you hear it.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's one less voice in the Haunt.

I can hear the wind out there now, and I'd forgotten what it sounded like.

quests.title: Farmer Felstone
quests.description: Kill Farmer Felstone and the Felstone Ghouls who work his field.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Captain Vance, and I run the patrols between here and Andorhal, for what that's worth these days.

The man who owned Felstone Field still walks it. He was stubborn alive, they tell me, and he's worse dead. My patrols cut across his field to save an hour, and he's had three of them with a rusted scythe.

They call him Farmer Felstone. Put him in the ground he wouldn't leave, and his Felstone Ghouls with him. Felstone Field's north of the crossroads. Look for the one with the scythe, and bring somebody, because he's tougher than his hands.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the field's quiet, for once.

I'd have bought grain off him, once. I suppose that's the Plaguelands for you.

quests.title: The Ghost in the Barn
quests.description: Kill the Dalson Ghost in the Dalson barn and the Dalson's Skeletons in its yard.
quests.accept_text:
Nobody goes into the Dalson barn. I lost a patrol in there. The one who came out said it was the father, Joseph Dalson, still looking for his family. He said it wasn't angry, it was looking, and it killed them anyway.

The Dalson Ghost keeps the barn and Dalson's Skeletons keep the yard. I want it ended, and I'd like it ended gently, if there's a gentle way.

It's the red barn on the Dalson farm. The skeletons walk the yard. The ghost won't come out, so you'll have to go in.
quests.turn_in_text:
He's at rest, then. I hope he found them.

Some things out here make you remember you were alive once. That was one of them.

quests.title: Snapjaw Shell
quests.description: Take Snapjaw Shell Plates from the Darrowmere Snapjaws at Darrowmere Lake.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Surgeon Grey. Mind the bucket.

When the fields take a leg off one of the Deathguard, I put it back, and I brace the break with turtle shell. It's hard as iron and it doesn't rot, which is more than I can say for anything else out here. The best shell in the Plaguelands is on the Darrowmere Snapjaws at the lake.

They sun themselves on the shore south of the old Sorrow Hill road. Go for the legs, because you won't cut through the shell. That's the whole point of it. Bring me plates, and the bigger the better.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at the grain on that. That'll hold a femur together for a hundred years.

There's an old one at the lake I've wanted for a long time.

quests.title: Old Darrowjaw
quests.description: Kill Old Darrowjaw and the Darrowmere Snapjaws round him at Darrowmere Lake.
quests.accept_text:
The oldest snapjaw in Darrowmere Lake has a name. Old Darrowjaw's been in that water since before the plague, and his shell would brace a wall, never mind a leg. I've wanted it for years.

He's a big turtle and a very bad-tempered one, and the Darrowmere Snapjaws keep close to him.

He keeps to the deep end and comes up when he likes. Thin the young ones while you wait. When he pulls you under, fight your way back to the shore and don't panic. Panicking is how I get most of my patients.
quests.turn_in_text:
Now that's a shell, a real one.

I'll have the whole Deathguard braced by spring. The newcomers across the street keep asking me how we stay on our feet, and now I'll have something to show them.

quests.title: What We Kill
quests.description: Kill Scarlet Outriders and Scarlet Field Chaplains on the north side of Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Rory Callahan. Before you wear our flame, you need to know the one rule, so here it is. We kill the mindless dead and the fanatics who burn people, and nobody else.

I wore the red for a year. When the world ended the Crusade were the only ones killing what was killing us, and I joined them. Then I saw who else they were burning, people like me, for the crime of being born on Earth. I scraped the red off and walked out, and some good people walked out with me.

The Scarlet Outriders and the Scarlet Field Chaplains patrol the north side of Andorhal now. That's who we kill. Don't touch the Forsaken. They're rude, and they're not mindless.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the work, and some days I can live with it.

I laid steel in Boston for twenty years. I'd still rather be doing that.

quests.title: Red on the Road
quests.description: Take a set of Scarlet Patrol Orders from a Scarlet Field Chaplain in Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
The Crusade doesn't send chaplains this far south unless it's planning something. The Scarlet Field Chaplains in Andorhal carry their orders from Hearthglen, and I want to read them.

Bring me a set with the seal unbroken. I want to know whose seal is on them before I see what it says. I know most of the hands in Hearthglen. I used to take orders from them.

The chaplains work the north side of Andorhal and keep their orders in a satchel. Don't open it.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's Hearthglen's seal, and it's signed by Victor Hale himself.

He was a security contractor back home. I served beside him, God help me. If he's sending orders this far south, the Pale Watch needs to know.

quests.title: Hearthglen's Road
quests.description: Carry the Crusade's orders to Watch Captain Lena Fischer at the Pale Watch, off the King's Road in North WPL.

objectives.label: Bring the Crusade's orders to Watch Captain Lena Fischer at the Pale Watch

quests.accept_text:
These orders say the Crusade's moving more patrols down the road from Hearthglen. We keep a town on that road. The Pale Watch, under Watch Captain Lena Fischer. It's close enough to Hearthglen that they can see each other's fires.

I want this in Lena's hands before Hale's patrols are on her doorstep.

Go out the east gate and north up the King's Road, through the gate at the top of the fields, and keep on toward Hearthglen. The Pale Watch's gate is off the road where it starts to climb. Lena will be the one shouting.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's Hale's seal, of course it is.

I was a police officer in Hamburg, back home, and I know what a man looks like when he's getting ready to do something terrible. Stay a while. I could use you up here.

on_accept.name: Hale's Orders
on_accept.description: The Crusade's orders from Hearthglen, still sealed, wrapped in oilcloth by Rory.

quests.title: The Groundskeeper
quests.description: Kill the Groundskeeper and the Caer Darrow Ghouls on Caer Darrow.
quests.accept_text:
Across Darrowmere Lake there's an island, Caer Darrow, and Scholomance lies under it. The Cult teaches necromancy there to anyone who asks, and plenty ask.

I want eyes on that island. Right now the Groundskeeper keeps it, a dead man with a spade, and the Caer Darrow Ghouls dig wherever he points.

Caer Darrow's in the east of the lake. Cross the causeway. He walks the grounds and the ghouls dig for him, and he's strong, so take friends. When he's gone, the Order can sit on Scholomance's doorstep and watch who goes in.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the island's watched, and the Cult knows it.

Scholomance can wait. We'll be ready for it when it's time.

quests.title: Steel for the Order
quests.description: Take Rusted Andorhal Blades from the Andorhal Skeletons in Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Kofi Mensah. I train the recruits, the ones who walked out of the Crusade and the ones who came through with nothing, and the recruits keep breaking their swords.

The Andorhal Skeletons carry the old Lordaeron infantry's blades. Rory says the steel under the rust is better than anything we can buy, and Rory knows steel. I'd rather my people swung a dead man's good sword than a live man's bad one.

The skeletons are all over Andorhal and most still carry a blade. Don't clean them. Bring them back rusted and Rory will make them good again.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's a month of drills that won't end with somebody holding half a sword.

I taught PE in Kumasi, back home. This is the same job, mostly, with more swords.

quests.title: Archers on the Wall
quests.description: Kill Andorhal Skeletal Archers on Andorhal's walls.
quests.accept_text:
I take the recruits into Andorhal to learn. It's the best classroom in the Plaguelands, and the worst. The Andorhal Skeletal Archers on the broken walls keep putting arrows into my students, and half of those students came through in the Integration and had never seen a bow before last spring.

Clear the walls before the next lesson. Close the distance fast, because they won't. When you're done, I'll bring the recruits and they can learn from somebody who isn't shooting at them.
quests.turn_in_text:
They came back with no arrows in them today. That's a first.

There's something bigger in the city, and I'd like it gone too.

quests.title: The Abominations
quests.description: Kill Andorhal Abominations in Andorhal and cut out their Abomination Stitching.
quests.accept_text:
The Andorhal Abominations are the Scourge's stitched brutes, sewn together from whatever was lying around. My recruits see one and forget everything I've taught them.

I want them dead, and I want their stitching. The thread that holds them together is tougher than wire, and our armourers can use it to bind plate.

They lumber round the middle of Andorhal. They're slow and they hit like a cart. Cut the thread out afterward, and wash your hands before you eat. Priya will check.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's some ugly thread. Thank you, I think.

The recruits can do the rest of Andorhal. You've earned a rest.

quests.title: Shades of Caer Darrow
quests.description: Destroy the Caer Darrow Shades on Caer Darrow and the water round it.
quests.accept_text:
When Rory sent scouts toward Caer Darrow, the Caer Darrow Shades came off the island and over the water after them. I lost a recruit that night, a girl called Teodora. She was nineteen.

I'd like them destroyed. I won't pretend it's for the Order.

The shades drift on the island in the east of the lake and on the water round it. They're cold to the touch, so wrap up warm, and don't let them get behind you.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's for Teodora. She'd only been here since the Integration, and she was braver than I was at her age.

Thank you. I'll tell the recruits who did it.

quests.title: Uther's Rest
quests.description: Visit Uther's Tomb, south of the old Sorrow Hill road in South WPL.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Odile Marchand. I keep the Order's chapel, and before that I kept Uther's Tomb.

We built our fort on Sorrow Hill because of the tomb. The Lightbringer is buried there. When the hill got too dead to hold, we came here, but the tomb didn't come with us, and somebody has to remember it.

Go and stand at it before you do anything else for the Order. Take the road south from the crossroads, past the graves on the hill. The tomb's at the foot of the hill, with the statue. It's still the quietest place in the Plaguelands, and I think it's the only one.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's quiet there, isn't it? Even the dead keep away.

I taught history in Lyon, back on Earth. I never thought I'd be keeping a legend's grave.

quests.title: Laid to Rest
quests.description: Kill Dalson's Ghouls and Dalson's Skeletons on the Dalson farm.
quests.accept_text:
The Dalsons' farmhands never got a burial. They got up instead, and now Dalson's Ghouls and Dalson's Skeletons work that farm for the Scourge.

I'd like them put down. And I'd like you to say a word for each of them, if you can manage it. It doesn't have to be a prayer. It doesn't have to be in any language they'd know.

The Dalson farm's north of the road, with the red barn. The ghouls work the yard and the skeletons walk the fields. Say whatever you like over them. It's the saying that matters.
quests.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I've added their names to the chapel's book, the ones we know.

There's somewhere worse than Dalson's, and I'd like you to see it.

quests.title: The Haunt's Banshees
quests.description: Kill Haunt Banshees and Writhing Crypt Fiends at the Writhing Haunt.
quests.accept_text:
On still nights on Sorrow Hill I could hear the Writhing Haunt. I can't hear it from here, behind the wall, and I'm ashamed of how glad I am.

The Haunt Banshees wail over that farm, and the Writhing Crypt Fiends dig under it. The sound gets into the stones, and into the people who live near them.

It's east of Dalson's, where the trees die. The banshees drift and the fiends come up out of the ground. Cover your ears if it helps. I want it quiet.
quests.turn_in_text:
Somebody rode in from the east today and said they could hear the wind out there.

Thank you. Rest here, if you like. The chapel's warm.

quests.title: Darrowmere's Drowned
quests.description: Kill Drowned Lakewalkers on the shores of Darrowmere Lake.
quests.accept_text:
I used to walk down to Darrowmere Lake in the evenings, and the Drowned Lakewalkers walked up out of it to meet me. They're the people of Caer Darrow, I think. They went into the water when the plague crossed the lake and they never came out.

I'd like them laid to rest, and I'd like the shore safe for the Order's scouts.

Go south and east, past the tomb to the lake. They come out of the shallows. Stay on the shore if you can, because they're stronger in the water.
quests.turn_in_text:
I'll say their names tonight, the ones Ser Aldren remembers.

We had a lake at home too, Lac d'Annecy. I swam in it every summer. I don't think I'll swim in this one.

quests.title: Bear Stew
quests.description: Take Plague-Free Bear Flanks from the Diseased Black Bears along the King's Road.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Priya, and I cook for the Order, and the Order's eaten the last of the meat.

The Diseased Black Bears out there are sick, but not all the way through. I've found that a cut from the back of the leg comes out clean, if you're careful and you're quick. It's not the worst thing I've cooked here. It's not even the worst thing I've cooked this week.

The bears keep to the trees along the King's Road, east of the gate. Cut from the back of the leg, where it's still red. If it's grey, leave it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Oh, that's lovely, that's dinner for a week.

I ran a guesthouse in Kochi, and my mother's curry was the reason people came back. It works on bear, it turns out. She'd laugh herself silly.

quests.title: Letters Home
quests.description: Carry the bundle of letters to Dr. Hannah Lindqvist at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon.

objectives.label: Bring the bundle of letters to Dr. Hannah Lindqvist at Sun Rock Retreat

quests.accept_text:
Nobody knows where anybody ended up after the Integration. We write letters anyway. Half of them are addressed to a name and a guess.

I keep the Order's bundle. There's a geologist at Sun Rock Retreat in Stonetalon, Dr. Hannah Lindqvist, who keeps a list of every name she's heard from Kalimdor's camps. If anyone's going to match a letter to a person, it's her.

Go back through Tirisfal, take the zeppelin to Orgrimmar and a wind rider to Sun Rock. Hannah's the one with the maps of the volcano. Please don't lose any of them. Some of them took people a month to write.
quests.turn_in_text:
So many of them. Let me see whose names I've got.

There's one here for a woman in Ratchet I wrote down last month. I'll make sure this gets to her. That's one, at least.

on_accept.name: Bundle of Letters
on_accept.description: A thick bundle of letters tied with kitchen string, addressed to people nobody has seen in three years.

quests.title: Clear Skies
quests.description: Kill Plaguewing Vultures over South WPL's fields.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Anders, and these are the Order's hawks. They carry our letters now that we've given up flying people.

The Plaguewing Vultures have started going after them in the air. I've lost two birds this week, and one of them was carrying a letter I'd rather the Crusade didn't read.

The vultures circle over everything dead, which out here is most of the map. Shoot them down if you can. Don't let them settle anywhere near the wall.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's much better, and my birds will fly tomorrow.

I kept pigeons in Bergen when I was a boy, back on Earth. Hawks are harder, and they're worth it.

quests.title: Jesses for the Hawks
quests.description: Take Clean Wolf Sinew from the Plague-Ridden Wolves in the fields.
quests.accept_text:
I tie the hawks with jesses, leather straps on their legs, and the plague rots leather in a week. Sinew doesn't rot the way leather does.

The Plague-Ridden Wolves in the fields carry good sinew under the rot, if you cut carefully. Not every wolf will have any worth taking.

They run the grass either side of the King's Road. Cut from the back legs, where the plague's slowest. Bring me enough to rig every bird I have.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's good sinew, and that's every bird tied properly.

We used gut string for the pigeons when I was a boy. It turns out it's the same knot.

quests.title: Eyes on Andorhal
quests.description: Look over the middle of Andorhal and report back to Agata.

objectives.label: Look over the middle of Andorhal

quests.accept_text:
I'm Agata Wrobel. I'm back on my feet after a week in a cell under the Scarlet Monastery, and I want to work. Rory says not alone yet, so you can be my eyes.

Rory wants to know where the Crusade's patrols cross the Scourge's in Andorhal. I want you to walk into the middle of the city, by the old town hall, and look round. Count the red and count the dead. Then get out.

Andorhal's south of the crossroads. Don't stop to fight anything you don't have to. The point is to come back.
quests.turn_in_text:
So it's red to the north and dead to the south, and they meet in the square. That's useful to know.

I was a mountain guide in the Tatras, back home. Getting people in and out of places is the only thing I was ever good at.

quests.title: The Survey Map
quests.description: Take the Andorhal Survey Map from a Scarlet Outrider in Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
The Crusade's Scarlet Outriders carry a surveyor's map of Andorhal. One of the guards at the Monastery bragged about it while I was in the cell, so I know it's real. Every Scourge strong point is on it, and every Forsaken one too.

If the Crusade knows where everyone is, so should we.

The outriders patrol the north side of Andorhal. One of them carries it rolled in a leather tube. Bring it back dry, and don't let them burn it. They burn things when they're losing.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at this. They've marked the Bulwark's patrols to the hour.

Rory needs to see this, and then Venn does, whether she likes us or not.

quests.title: The Fallen of Andorhal
quests.description: Take Andorhal Company Rings from the Andorhal Skeletons in the west of Andorhal.
quests.accept_text:
Ser Aldren Holt. I held Andorhal for the King, and then I held it for the Crusade, and I walked out of both.

When the plague came, my company held the west end of the city. My men are the Andorhal Skeletons now. Some of them still wear the company's iron rings.

I'd like the rings back. I can't bury the men, so I'll bury those by Uther's Tomb. Not all of them will still have one. Bring me what you find, and forgive me for asking. I don't ask lightly.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's Corporal Brask's, and that's Hask's, and this one was little Tom Barrow's. He lied about his age.

I'll bury them by the tomb in the morning. Thank you. I mean that more than you know.

quests.title: The Necrolytes
quests.description: Kill Cauldron Necrolytes at the Dalson farm.
quests.accept_text:
I buried my company's rings by the tomb, and then I asked who raised my men in the first place. The answer's the Cauldron Necrolytes at the Dalson farm. They learned their trade in Andorhal, on my people.

I want them dead. I won't dress it up, because it's personal.

They stir the cauldron in the Dalson yard, north of the road. They'll raise anything that falls near them, so draw them away from the ghouls before you start.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's some justice, at least. Not much, but some.

The Crusade told me this would feel like holiness. It feels like tidying up.

quests.title: Under the Haunt
quests.description: Kill Writhing Burrowers and Brood Guardians in the Writhing Deep, under the Writhing Haunt.
quests.accept_text:
I've been watching the Writhing Haunt for the Order. There's a hole behind it the crypt fiends keep crawling in and out of. I went down far enough to know it doesn't stop.

It's a web of tunnels, and they all lead back to the middle. The Writhing Burrowers come up out of the floor and the Brood Guardians stand over the passages like they're guarding a nursery, which I think they are.

The cave mouth is behind the Haunt, east of the road. Thin them out so we can see what's at the bottom, and keep your back to a wall.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the outer burrows quiet, then.

I used to take tourists down caves in the Tatras, and not one of them ever tried to eat me. There's a chamber in the middle that everything was guarding, and I think we both know what's in it.

quests.title: The Broodlord
quests.description: Kill Broodlord Szarak and the Silken Bride in the Writhing Deep.
quests.accept_text:
In the middle of the Writhing Deep, where every tunnel meets, Broodlord Szarak sits on the brood. Off the north rim there's a pocket of web I won't go near, and something lives in it the fiends call The Silken Bride.

I want them both dead before the brood hatches. If that nest opens, the Haunt will be the least of anyone's problems.

The broodlord's in the chamber in the middle. The bride's up in the north-east, at the end of a tunnel off the outer ring. Bring something for poison, because she bites and it doesn't wear off.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then that's the brood finished, and the Haunt's lost its nursery.

I've been in a cell and I've been in a web now. I'm not sure which I liked less. Here, take this. You've earned it.

quests.title: Samples for the Bulwark
quests.description: Carry Marwen's reagent case to Apothecary Dorian Vesk at the Bulwark, on the road east from Tirisfal.

objectives.label: Bring Marwen's reagent case to Apothecary Dorian Vesk at the Bulwark

quests.accept_text:
I've read every report the Bulwark's sent back to the Undercity, and I don't believe half of them. Dorian Vesk says the plague in the western fields has changed. Dorian has said a great many things.

So I've packed him a case of clean reagents, enough for every test he'll need, and if he's right, he can prove it.

Go up through the Ruins and east across Tirisfal to the wall at the end of the road. That's the Bulwark. He keeps the vats by the east gate. Don't open the case. I've counted every vial, and I'll know.
quests.turn_in_text:
Marwen's actually sent me clean reagents, and I didn't think she had any.

She thinks I'm wrong about the plague. She'll read my next report a lot more carefully once these tell her I'm right. Stay a while, because the fields need hands more than I need a courier.

on_accept.name: Marwen's Reagent Case
on_accept.description: A small locked case of glass vials packed in straw, every one labelled in a precise hand.

quests.title: Hands for the Order
quests.description: Carry the Order's notice to Drillmaster Kofi Mensah in the Order's quarter of the Bulwark.

objectives.label: Bring the Order's notice to Drillmaster Kofi Mensah at the Bulwark

quests.accept_text:
You look like you can swing something heavy, which is what I need. I've a notice to send on, and I've been crying it twice a day for a month.

The Order of the Pale Flame wants fighters. They're camped inside the Bulwark now, at the end of the road east, and they don't care where anyone was born. I don't know much about them, and the Deathguard say less, but they pay and they feed you.

Take this to their drillmaster, Kofi Mensah. Go east through Tirisfal to the wall. Their banners are on the south side of the street, and Kofi will be in the yard shouting at somebody.
quests.turn_in_text:
So Wexley sent you with the notice. He cries it twice a day in Brill, and nobody's told him to stop yet.

I'm glad you came. Half my recruits walked out of the Crusade and the other half walked in off the road, so you'll fit in whatever you are. Go and see Rory when you've found a bunk.

on_accept.name: The Order's Notice
on_accept.description: A notice in a firm hand under a pale flame: fighters wanted at the Bulwark, no questions asked about where you were born.

quests.title: A Chaplain's Letter
quests.description: Carry Chaplain Blackwood's letter to Chaplain Odile Marchand at the Order's chapel in the Bulwark.

objectives.label: Bring Chaplain Blackwood's letter to Chaplain Odile Marchand at Uther's Tomb

quests.accept_text:
I still pray in Tarren Mill, most days to an empty chapel. I've heard there's another chaplain who still prays, a woman called Odile Marchand who kept Uther's Tomb for the Order of the Pale Flame.

I've written her a letter. I've never met her, and I think that's the best reason to write.

The road north is shut, so go round through Tirisfal and east to the Bulwark. The Order keeps a chapel inside the wall, on the south side. I'd take it myself, but somebody's got to keep this door open.
quests.turn_in_text:
A letter from Tarren Mill, from a chaplain I've never met.

He asks whether I'm afraid the Light will stop answering. I'm not, and I'm going to write back and tell him so properly. Thank you for carrying it all this way.

on_accept.name: Chaplain Blackwood's Letter
on_accept.description: A letter sealed with plain candle wax, addressed in careful capitals to the chaplain at Uther's Tomb.

quests.title: The School Under the Island
quests.description: Kill Darkmaster Gandling in the lower halls of Scholomance, on the island in Darrowmere.
quests.accept_text:
You've seen the island in Darrowmere, the one with the dead trees and the lit windows. That's Caer Darrow. The Barovs owned it, and then they sold it to the Cult of the Damned for a promise, and now it's a school. The Scourge teach necromancy there the way my old trade school taught welding.

The headmaster is Darkmaster Gandling. Every necromancer who's put a skeleton back on its feet in Andorhal learned it in his halls. We can kill students until the lake freezes over and he'll keep making more.

He keeps his study at the bottom of the school, below everything else. You won't get there alone, so don't try. Take your whole company, and come back and tell me the school's closed.
quests.turn_in_text:
The school's closed, then. They'll open it again one day, they always do, but not this year.

I came through in the Integration with a welding ticket and a bad knee. I never thought I'd be shutting down schools.

quests.title: The Barovs
quests.description: Kill Lord Alexei Barov and Lady Illucia Barov in Scholomance.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Aldren Holt, knight of the Pale Flame, for whatever that's worth to you. I want to tell you about a family.

The Barovs owned Caer Darrow, and when the plague came they sold it to the Cult for eternal life. They got it. Lord Alexei Barov and Lady Illucia Barov still walk their own vault under the school, dead and proud of it, and they still think the island's theirs.

I've read their family's letters. They sold their tenants along with the land, and the tenants are in the ossuary now. Put the Barovs in the ground with them. They're always together, so plan for both.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's good work. I'll write it down in the Order's book, under the tenants' names, so they're the ones remembered.

Back home I'd have called this justice. Here I just call it Tuesday.

quests.title: The Cult's Classroom
quests.description: Kill Instructor Malicia and Scholomance Necromancers in the lower halls of Scholomance.
quests.accept_text:
It's Rook again. The Cult's letters I've been breaking all season come from one place, and it's a classroom.

Instructor Malicia teaches the Scholomance Necromancers how to raise the dead and how to write in cipher, and she's better at the second than the first. Every courier you killed in the south carried her lessons.

Go down into the lower halls and end the lesson. Kill her students on the way. I'd like the Cult to find its next letter much harder to write, and I'd like to read it anyway.
quests.turn_in_text:
Her notes are in a cipher I haven't seen before, which is lovely. I'll be up all night, and I don't sleep anyway.

I'll send a copy across the street to the Order. They've earned it, and so have you.

quests.title: Frostwhisper's Laboratory
quests.description: Kill Ras Frostwhisper in the upper halls of Scholomance.
quests.accept_text:
I'm Surgeon Grey. I put the Deathguard back together, and I can tell you whose work it's been when a dead thing won't stay dead.

Ras Frostwhisper keeps a laboratory in the upper halls of the school. He was a wizard once, and now he's a lich, and he's teaching the Cult how to keep a corpse cold and fresh and walking. I've pulled his ice out of three abominations this month.

Go into his laboratory and break him. Liches don't like to stay broken, so make a thorough job of it, and then break his bench too.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then that's one less hand stitching what I've got to unstitch.

I kept a little of his frost in a jar, for study. Don't tell the High Executor.
